result.question: Distinguish between revenue deficit, fiscal deficit and primary deficit. Why is the composition of the fiscal deficit as important as its size? (Answer in 150 words)

sentences.text: Budget deficits show how far government spending exceeds its receipts and what the gap finances.
Revenue deficit is the excess of revenue receipts over revenue expenditure.
A revenue deficit means the government is dissaving and borrowing to meet part of its consumption expenditure.
Fiscal deficit is the excess of total expenditure over total receipts excluding borrowings, and it shows the government's total borrowing requirement from all sources.
Primary deficit is the fiscal deficit minus capital expenditure, so it reflects only the borrowing needed for creating new assets.
Composition matters because borrowing for capital expenditure creates assets that raise future growth and help service debt.
When borrowing funds salaries, subsidies and interest, debt and interest liabilities build up without matching assets.
Hence a large share of revenue deficit in the fiscal deficit signals that loans are financing consumption rather than investment.
Fiscal consolidation under the FRBM framework should therefore aim not only at a smaller deficit but at a higher share of capital outlay within it.
